subject: Architecture
title: The Taj Mahal: A Monument to Grief
description: Learn The Taj Mahal: A Monument to Grief in one minute.

hook.text: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his wife, who died giving birth to their 14th child.

buildup.text: Twenty thousand workers spent 22 years building it from white marble inlaid with 28 gemstones.

discovery.text: The minarets lean slightly outward so that in an earthquake, they fall away from the tomb.

twist.text: Shah Jahan planned a matching black marble tomb for himself across the river. It was never built.

climax.text: His own son imprisoned him. He spent his last years gazing at the Taj from a window.

punchline.text: He built the world's most beautiful building. Then lost everything.

quiz.question: Why do the Taj Mahal's minarets lean outward?
options: A construction error that was never corrected
So they fall away from the tomb during an earthquake
To create an optical illusion of greater height

details.summary: The Taj Mahal, built between 1632 and 1653 by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, combines Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural traditions into a symmetrical complex centered on a white marble mausoleum.
details.whyItMatters: The Taj Mahal proves that architecture born from emotion can achieve universal beauty. Built as an expression of personal grief, it transcended its origin to become a global symbol of love and one of humanity's greatest architectural achievements.
takeaways: Built 1632-1653 as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal by Shah Jahan
Combines Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural traditions
White marble, gemstone inlay, and proportional perfection define it

faq.question: How many workers built the Taj Mahal?
faq.answer: An estimated 20,000 laborers and artisans worked on the complex over 21 years. Specialists came from across the Mughal Empire and beyond — marble carvers from Bukhara, calligraphers from Persia and Syria, and inlay workers from Southern India who embedded precious stones into marble.

faq.question: Why does the Taj Mahal change color?
faq.answer: The white Makrana marble is semi-translucent and reflects surrounding light. It appears pink at dawn, white during midday, golden at sunset, and silvery under moonlight. This was likely intentional — the changing appearance symbolizes the transient nature of earthly beauty.
